name: Teaching Textbooks
line: Teaching Textbooks teaches lesson by lesson, in a fixed order. In AMP, every answer sets the next problem.
description: AMP vs Teaching Textbooks: lessons in a fixed order, each opened by a lecture. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Teaching Textbooks is a course of lessons in a fixed order. Each lesson opens with a narrated lecture and then a problem set, and the adult picks the level with a placement test [2][3][4]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous: every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem. In Teaching Textbooks the adult prints a placement test, gives it and scores it, and the company calls its pass guidelines "very rough" [4]. The learner then takes the course's lessons in order [2][7].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem in front of the learner: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Teaching Textbooks the unit is the lesson: an animated, narrated lecture, then a problem set, with a quiz about every seventh lesson [2][3][7]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [12].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP a skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. An answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count. Repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. Teaching Textbooks keeps a running course average, and the next lesson in the sequence comes next [2][3][7]. Its gradebook notes where a learner used a hint, a second try or a solution [3][7].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Every answer sets the next problem, and that problem can be an old skill due back. Teaching Textbooks mixes earlier topics into every assignment, in the same course order for every student [2]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [11].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math, from counting through precalculus in one program. A learner further along in geometry than in fractions gets work at both levels. Teaching Textbooks runs from Math 3 to Pre-Calculus as separate courses, each its own app, and a course covers one level [1][2][6].

rows.range: Math 3 through Pre-Calculus, one course at a time, each its own app [1][6].
rows.start: A printable placement test the adult gives and scores, with pass guidelines the company calls very rough [4].
rows.teaching: A narrated, animated lecture opens each lesson. Problems are read aloud, many have hints, and each has a step-by-step video solution [1][2][7].
rows.next: The next lesson in a fixed order, the same for every student [2][7].
rows.mastery: A running course average, with a quiz about every seventh lesson [3][7].
rows.review: Earlier topics mixed into every assignment, in the same course order for every student [2].
rows.print: The course's eBook, printable from the parent portal, the same for every student. A printed textbook with answer key is also offered [2][5].
rows.adult: Gives the placement test, sets a start date, then follows the gradebook and a daily progress email [2][4][7].
rows.reports: A gradebook by lesson that shows hint use, second attempts and solution views, plus a daily progress email [3][7].
rows.evidence: No outcome study on its site, and no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [1][8][9][10].

theirs: Teaching Textbooks is a series of math courses, from Math 3 through Pre-Calculus. Each course is its own app and covers one level [1][2][6].

The adult chooses the level with a printable placement test [4]. The learner then works through the course's lessons in order. Each lesson opens with an animated, narrated lecture, followed by a problem set that mixes new and earlier topics [2][3]. Every problem is read aloud and graded on entry. A wrong answer gets a second chance, and a step-by-step video solution is there after the answer [1][2]. A quiz comes about every seventh lesson [7].
credit: Earlier topics come back in every assignment [2].
A step-by-step solution for every problem, after it is answered [1][2].
A narrated lecture for every lesson, with the learner answering along the way [3][7].

theirs: We found no study of how much students learn with Teaching Textbooks. Its site has no research page, and its reviews page holds parent testimonials [1][8]. It has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [9][10].
ours: The two findings that bear most on this comparison: practice that mixes and spaces topics scored 62% against 38% for practice in blocks a month later, on the researchers' own test, in a randomized trial that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations [11]; and worked examples improve math performance across 55 studies [12]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: You want each lesson to open with a narrated lecture before the problems.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no placement test.
You want each next problem chosen from your child's own answers.
You want repeated misses to lead back to what a skill builds on.
Your child is at different levels in different parts of math.
You want one program from counting through precalculus.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Teaching Textbooks?
questions.answer: Teaching Textbooks teaches in lessons, in a fixed order, each opened by a narrated lecture [2][3]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Teaching Textbooks work?
questions.answer: We found no study of how much students learn with it, and it has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [9][10].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
